department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

deadline.value: December 15 for Fall 2027, international and Canadian applicants.
deadline.quote: Application Deadline - International | FALL September 15 December 15 December 15

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

gre_general.value: Not mandatory; you may send scores if you have them.
gre_general.quote: Submission of GRE (General Aptitude Test) scores is not mandatory. Applicants who have written the GRE are welcome to submit their scores for consideration.

supervisor.value: You don't need a supervisor before applying; emailing potential supervisors is optional.
supervisor.quote: Is it mandatory to find a supervisor before applying for admission? | No, you may email potential supervisors (see Research Areas) if you wish, but it is not required.

funding.value: Funding comes from the department, the Faculty and GPS, but no guarantee is stated.
funding.quote: Funding for graduate students is available from the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, the Faculty of Engineering and the Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies Office.

entry_route.value: PhD applicants must hold a suitable master's degree.
entry_route.quote: Applicants to the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) program, in addition to satisfying the admission requirements for the MSc or MEng program, must hold a suitable Master's degree from a recognized university.

toefl_min.value: TOEFL iBT 100 with at least 20 in each section.
toefl_min.quote: iBT (internet based test) - overall score of 100 (no less than 20 in each of the four component scores)

ielts_min.value: IELTS 7.0 overall with at least 6.0 in each band.
ielts_min.quote: IELTS (International English Language Testing System) - overall band score of 7.0 or greater (no less than 6.0 in each of the four individual component scores)
